correctness.rationale: For indexed y, a fixed state at the cut before site 0 extends by the displayed backward maps to an n-periodic sequence of overlapping four-bit states. Taking first coordinates of those states recovers a unique predecessor, and overlap enforces wraparound even for n<5. Independent enumeration directly from the polynomial gives 491 maps (ranks 16,10,8,6,4: 1,2,2,6,480); all sixteen length-four products have rank four. Left composition preserves the kernel when rank stays four, and the 480 maps divide into two closed kernel classes of 240. Each has ten four-point images, each image meets each kernel block once, and each fiber contains every one of the 24 possible block-to-image bijections. A fixed point must lie in the image, on which the map acts as a permutation, so three fixed points are excluded. The n=1,2,3 count vectors in order (0,1,2,4) are (1,0,1,0), (3,0,0,1), (1,6,1,0). Both classes are strongly connected and have coprime return walks of lengths 2 and 11. A block relabelling commutes with the left-composition transition and is transitive on each image fiber; uniqueness of the stationary distribution in a class forces uniformity conditional on the image. Each fiber gives (9,8,6,1)/24. Therefore the possibly unequal stationary class weights do not matter, and primitive finite-chain convergence gives an O(rho^n) error for some rho<1. The reverse evaluation order does not alter sampling for iid uniform letters. The result is for period dividing n, not least period n or rotation classes; finite direct checks alone do not prove the limit.
